question: priorities
notes: No customers or compliance rules here. I did weigh tradeoffs though, every checkov skip in lab 07 has a reason written next to it.

question: ops-model
notes: I'm the only person so I own all of it. Every resource has a Lab tag. There are no teams to agree anything with.

question: org-culture
notes: One person, no organization.

question: observability
notes: Detailed monitoring was switched on but I never defined what healthy means or looked at a metric. Lab 11 is for this.

question: dev-integ
notes: Terraform in git with fmt, validate and checkov on every push. Applying is still by hand from CloudShell, and there's only one environment. Nothing patches the instances on a schedule.

question: mit-deploy-risks
notes: The rolling update starts new instances before removing old ones and I watched it with a curl loop. There's no automatic rollback if a bad version goes out, and I never tested going back.

question: ready-to-support
notes: The README works as a runbook and I read terraform plan before every apply. No playbook for when something breaks.

question: workload-observability
notes: No alarms, no dashboard, no logs. I only found out about the 502s because I was running curl myself.

question: operations-health
notes: Nothing measured here.

question: event-response
notes: Auto Scaling replacing a broken instance is an automated response. That's the only one, nobody gets told when it happens.

question: evolve-ops
notes: Every lab has a What Broke section with the actual cause, and it's all public. No metrics to review and no regular process, this review is the first time I've gone back over a lab.

question: securely-operate
notes: Root has MFA and no keys from lab 01, and checkov runs in CI. Everything is in one account, and I never did a threat model.

question: identities
notes: MFA on root and my admin user, an Admins group, no access keys. CloudShell and the instance role both use temporary credentials. Lab 07 has no secrets to store, that part comes with the database lab.

question: permissions
notes: The instance role only has the Session Manager policy and Access Analyzer stays on. I'm not ticking least privilege because my own user has AdministratorAccess. Lab 14 looks at that.

question: detect-investigate-events
notes: CloudTrail goes to one bucket and the lab 02 alerts cover the account. The load balancer access logs and VPC flow logs were skipped in lab 07, so I can't see who actually hit the site.

question: network-protection
notes: Public and private subnets, security groups that reference each other, the default group locked, all of it in Terraform. No WAF, so nothing inspects the traffic.

question: protect-compute
notes: No SSH, only Session Manager, and instances get replaced instead of fixed. Inspector is blocked on the Free plan and nothing else scans them. The AMI is the stock Amazon Linux one.

question: data-classification
notes: The page only shows the version, the hostname and the AZ. There's no data to classify.

question: protect-data-rest
notes: The EBS volumes are encrypted with the default key. I don't manage any keys myself yet, that's lab 14.

question: protect-data-transit
notes: Plain HTTP the whole way because I have no domain and so no certificate. It's a gap for now.

question: incident-response
notes: I have alerts but no plan for what I'd do after one fires. Lab 15 is the drill for this.

question: application-security
notes: The page deploys through user data and CI checks the Terraform on every push. Those checks look at the infrastructure and not the app. Nobody reviews my code and I've never run a penetration test.

question: manage-service-limits
notes: I never looked at a single quota. Nothing hit one, but that's luck.

question: planning-network-topology
notes: The load balancer sits in two AZs and a /16 with /24 subnets leaves plenty of room. There's one VPC and nothing on premises, so the rest doesn't come up.

question: service-architecture
notes: It's one static page, there are no services to split up.

question: prevent-interaction-failure
notes: Nothing calls anything else apart from the load balancer calling the instances.

question: mitigate-interaction-failure
notes: The instances keep no state, which is why any of them can be thrown away. No throttling or retries anywhere.

question: monitor-aws-resources
notes: The metrics exist and the group acts on health checks by itself. No notifications go to me and no logs get analyzed.

question: adapt-to-changes
notes: It replaces broken instances by itself, both tests in lab 07 showed that. But there's no scaling policy, so max 4 does nothing outside a rolling update. More traffic gets no extra instances. Never load tested either.

question: tracking-change-management
notes: A new version means new instances, rolled out by the group. My tests were by hand, they aren't part of the deployment.

question: backing-up-data
notes: No data to back up, Terraform can rebuild all of it. This changes with the database lab.

question: fault-isolation
notes: Instances and load balancer are in two AZs, but the one NAT gateway is in 1a. If 1a goes down the site should still answer from 1b, but the 1b instance loses the internet and Session Manager.

question: withstand-component-failures
notes: Health checks every 10 seconds, traffic moves to the healthy instance and the group replaces the broken one. Healing only covers the instances, it won't bring back the NAT gateway's AZ. Nobody gets notified and there's no uptime target.

question: testing-resiliency
notes: I broke it on purpose in lab 07, but only once and by hand. I wrote up the causes, though the 3.5 minute wait for the replacement is still unexplained. No load test yet, so I don't know what it can take.

question: planning-for-recovery
notes: No recovery time or data loss target. Terraform rebuilds it in a few minutes, but the region and AZs are hard coded, so it can't simply move if us-east-1 is down.
